titles.en: Carved blocks of the Modelbook of the Three Rarities Hall

productionDate.eraLabel: 清乾隆十二年至十五年
productionDate.original: 乾隆十二年（1747）上谕，乾隆十五年（1750）刻跋
productionDate.note: The order dates from 1747 and the ministers' colophon from 1750; the intervening carving is not separately dated.

currentCollection.note: The Palace Museum states that the stones are set into the Yuegu Lou pavilion in Beihai Park; the press feature describes the two-storey building on the west slope of Qionghua Island. Neither source gives a block count that the other confirms.
currentCollection.noteZh: 故宫称帖石嵌于北海阅古楼；报道记该楼在琼岛西麓、上下两层。两处所记刻石方数互不印证。

provenanceEvents.summary: The Qianlong Emperor ordered the selection and carving of the imperial collection of calligraphy.
provenanceEvents.summaryZh: 乾隆帝特谕选编内府所藏法书，摹刻上石。

provenanceEvents.summary: A pavilion was built on the west slope of Qionghua Island to house the stones; its walls carry them today. The source dates the building, not the transfer of the stones.
provenanceEvents.summaryZh: 琼岛西麓建阅古楼以储帖石，今石仍嵌楼壁。所引来源记建楼之年，未记移石之年。

review.note: Draft object record. The stones are evidenced as a set in the pavilion's walls; no survey, block count or condition report is cited consistently. The stones were not examined.
review.noteZh: 草稿实物记录。帖石作为整组嵌于楼壁有据，但所引来源对石数、保存状况的记载不能互相印证。未实地核对。

notes: The object is the set of carved blocks, not any single rubbing. The Palace Museum's Qing rubbing is a separate object.
No block count is asserted: the press feature gives 495 and the museum entries give none, so the figure stays in the work notes as a reported number.
The stones are described as set into the walls of a building that is itself a heritage structure; the record makes no claim about public access or photography.
notesZh: 此件为整组刻石，非任何单一拓本；故宫藏清拓另作一件。
不主张石数：报道作四百九十五方，故宫条目未记，故该数字只作为转述留在作品说明中。
帖石嵌于同为文物建筑的楼壁；本记录不主张开放情况或可否摄影。
